Fashion designs can be protected under copyright law, but the protection is not automatic or all-encompassing. [d5] The U.S. [d5] Copyright Office confirms that fashion designs can qualify for copyright protection as 'graphic designs, artistic works, literary works, and works of artistic craftsmanship,' but only if they demonstrate a sufficient amount of creativity and originality [d5][d1]. However, the scope of this protection is limited — clothing is classified as a 'functional item' under the 1976 Copyright Act, and the Digital Millennium Copyright Act of 1998 further narrowed protection for fashion designs, making full copyright protection dependent on whether a design incorporates pictorial, graphic, or sculptural features that can be identified independently from its utilitarian aspects [d2][d3][d4].
[[END-OF-ANSWER]]
